core.title: Reference every convention node in at least one relationship edge
core.given: The repository has convention nodes (convention artifacts each carrying a rule id) and a directed relationship graph over those ids; this holds for all nodes, pre-existing or newly planned.
core.when: Relationship-graph coverage is evaluated, or you plan any change touching convention nodes or graph edges.
core.then: Ensure every non-excluded convention node's rule id appears as the source or target of at least one relationship-graph edge; a node referenced by no edge is an orphan and is refused.
prefer: For each orphan (new or pre-existing), author at least one edge with it as source or target, using a real relationship type/foundation to a semantically related node.
Plan the edge in the same change that introduces or renames a node.
avoid: Treating 'no dangling edges' as enough — the graph must cover every node.
Placeholder edges to unrelated nodes or with arbitrary type/foundation to silence the check.
Moving a real node into an excluded path or excluded id namespace to escape the check.
unless: The node lies in this check's excluded scope — excluded paths and excluded id namespaces — whose exact contents are owned by the stack realization.
core.why: Reverse half of graph integrity: the forward check forbids edges to missing nodes, this forbids nodes no edge reaches — no dangling edges AND no orphan nodes.
evidence: Graph-coverage check reports zero orphan nodes: every non-excluded convention rule id appears as the source or target of at least one edge in the relationship graph.
Each newly authored edge names a real relationship type/foundation and a semantically related counterpart node.
The forward check (no edge references a missing node) also passes.
verification: Node set: every convention artifact recognized by the profile's convention-node file pattern and carrying a rule id in the profile's convention-node identifier field (idiom.convention_node_id_field), excluding nodes in this check's excluded scope (excluded paths and id namespaces); the exact exclusion list is owned by the realization's checker, not the stack-wide scan-exclusion list. Evaluated over the whole graph, not just changed nodes.

Orphan: a convention node whose rule id (read via idiom.convention_node_id_field) is referenced by no edge endpoint (the profile's relationship-edge endpoint fields, idiom.relationship_edge_endpoints) in any relationship-graph edge.
The check targets the repository's directed convention-node relationship graph (located via the profile), whose edges connect node rule ids.
Orphans = node rule ids − (all edge sources ∪ all edge targets, both read via idiom.relationship_edge_endpoints); any non-empty result fails.
Severity 3; disposition strict: the rule fails on every finding; no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: orphan node — a non-excluded convention node referenced by no relationship-graph edge

fires: Graph validation finds a pre-existing non-excluded convention node referenced by no edge, even though the current plan adds, renames or removes no node or edge.
A plan adds a new convention node (a convention artifact carrying a rule id) but authors no relationship edge naming it.
A plan renames a convention's rule id and the edges still name only the old id.
A plan deletes the last relationship edge that referenced a given convention node.
doesNotFire: A convention node lies in this check's excluded paths.
A convention node's id lies in this check's excluded id namespaces.
A convention artifact that carries no rule id.
Every non-excluded node already appears as the source or target of at least one edge.

profileRequirements.meaning: How a convention-node artifact — a convention definition carrying a rule id, i.e. a node of the relationship graph — is recognized by file-name pattern.
The field of a convention-node artifact that carries the node's rule id — the identifier that relationship-graph edges reference.
The two relationship-graph edge fields that carry the source and target node identifiers.
Where the directed relationship graph that connects convention-node rule ids by edges lives.

proposedKeys.meaning: Name pattern(s) that identify a convention-node artifact: a convention definition carrying a rule id, which is a node of the relationship graph.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The suffix group's file_kind params (source, unit_test, acceptance_test, e2e_test, markup, plan_artifact, config) do not include the convention-definition artifact kind; no existing key says how a convention node is recognized.

proposedKeys.meaning: The field of a convention-node artifact that carries the node's rule id — the identifier that relationship-graph edges reference.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The idiom group covers handler, error, validation, import, markup and measurement constructs only; no key says which field of a convention artifact carries its graph identifier, so another stack cannot map the neutral 'rule id' onto its own schema.

proposedKeys.meaning: The relationship-graph edge fields that carry the source and target node identifiers.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The idiom group has no key for the relationship-graph artifact's edge schema; without it another stack cannot map the neutral 'source or target of an edge' onto its own edge fields.

proposedKeys.meaning: Location of the directed relationship graph whose edges connect convention-node rule ids.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The layout group covers wagon/feature/commons/plan-item/test locations only; no key locates the convention relationship-graph artifact.

bunOnly.reason: The authoring command is ATDD-Bun toolchain machinery; the edge-endpoint field names source_ref/target_ref reach the core through the profile key idiom.relationship_edge_endpoints, so only the command remains Bun-only.

bunOnly.text: Moving a real node under tests/fixtures or into demo.* to escape the check.
bunOnly.reason: The concrete excluded locations are this realization's rule-scoped exclusion list, owned by its checker; the core keeps the anti-pattern generically.

bunOnly.text: The node is under a path containing tests/fixtures or in the demo.* namespace — excluded.
bunOnly.reason: Rule-scoped exclusion values (paths and id namespaces) are realization data, not the stack-wide roots.excluded list; the core keeps the exception and defers the exact list to the realization.

bunOnly.reason: The rule-scoped exclusion values are owned by this realization's checker; the node file pattern and the identifier field reach the core through the profile keys suffix.convention_node and idiom.convention_node_id_field.

bunOnly.text: orphan_node: a convention node whose rule_id is referenced by no source_ref or target_ref in any relationship-graph edge.
bunOnly.reason: The finding/term id orphan_node is a realization label (the core names the check generically); the identifier and endpoint field names reach the core through the profile keys idiom.convention_node_id_field and idiom.relationship_edge_endpoints.

bunOnly.text: finding id `orphan_node`; graph-coverage detector computed as the set of non-excluded node rule_ids minus all edge source_ref/target_ref values, applied to the whole graph including pre-existing orphans.
bunOnly.reason: Finding and detector ids of this rule are realization details; the core fact names the finding generically, and the schema field names in the detector description reach the core via the profile keys idiom.convention_node_id_field and idiom.relationship_edge_endpoints.

neutralityNotes: This rule governs the ATDD convention graph itself, so 'convention node', 'rule id' and 'relationship graph' are treated as neutral ATDD artifact concepts rather than stack names. Four artifact facts could not be expressed with the closed vocabulary and are proposed: suffix.convention_node (node recognition pattern), idiom.convention_node_id_field (Bun: rule_id — how the neutral 'rule id' is represented), idiom.relationship_edge_endpoints (Bun: source_ref, target_ref — how the neutral 'source or target of an edge' is represented) and layout.convention_graph (graph location); the two idiom keys are referenced in node recognition and in the verification entries. This check's own exclusion scope (Bun: paths containing tests/fixtures and the demo.* id namespace) is rule-scoped, not the stack-wide roots.excluded list, so the core keeps the exception generically and defers the exact list to the realization's checker; the concrete values are recorded in bunOnly. Bun finding/term ids (orphan_node, relationship_graph), the `atdd author relationship` authoring command, and the validator/test reference are realization details and remain in bun.json as the worked example.
